g.text: Sync vs async replication, and why majority quorum prevents split-brain
SYNC: confirms only after a replica acks -- write is durable on 2 nodes before the client hears
success. Cost: every write pays the replica's round trip, permanently.
ASYNC: confirms before the replica has it. If the leader crashes between confirm and replicate,
that write is gone -- despite the client being told it succeeded. That's replication lag's real cost.
3 of 5 = MAJORITY -> can elect a new leader
Raft/Paxos rule: a decision is final only once a MAJORITY of all nodes agrees to it.
The 3-node side has a majority -- it can elect a new leader and keep accepting writes.
The 2-node side (with the old leader) can never reach majority while partitioned --
it can't confirm new writes as leader, so two conflicting leaders can never both be active.
